value.notes: The current value; there is no null/indeterminate mode.

Label/Track/Indicator.notes: Every Meter state type is an EMPTY object ({}) — unlike Progress there is no status state.

dataAttributes: None emitted by any Meter part (Progress has data-complete/data-indeterminate/data-progressing; Meter has no equivalent)

controlled.note: Display-only component; the surrounding app owns the value.

notableDifferences: React Aria has no Meter component, so this is a new primitive rather than a migration; the closest React Aria pattern is a ProgressBar with a static value (wrong role: progressbar vs meter).
Renders role="meter" with aria-valuemin/valuemax/valuenow/valuetext, so screen readers treat it as a gauge rather than a task progress indicator.
Zero data-attributes and empty state objects: no CSS state hooks are available (any dynamic styling must come from your own classes or the Value render prop).
Label renders role="presentation" and is wired through aria-labelledby.
